# The corpus: what hod has to compile

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask corpus census` from the captured corpus. Do not edit: run the command again. -->

The corpus is the LLVM IR that hod's front ends really produce, captured by `cargo xtask corpus capture` (`spec/harness.md`, "corpus") as `irdiff` tests: every module here was compiled by the real `llc`, linked and run, and the entry records what the program did. This report says what was captured and what was not, and counts the constructs of the captured modules. Counts are `occurrences (modules with at least one)`; a group is a source and the LLVM major whose tools produced and built it.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `marked-xfail` |  |  | 8 | 8 | the test's header says `xfail:`: kiln's own suite expects it to fail |
| `multi-file` | 59 | 59 | 119 | 118 | more than one translation unit built by one command (`module:`, `unit:`, `header-unit:`, `pch:` or `two-step:` in the header, or kiln++ ran llc more than once); for gcc-torture, a test in `builtins/` that is built with a second file |
| `needs-env` |  |  | 3 | 3 | the test needs an environment or input files the capture does not set up |
| `requires` |  |  | 38 | 75 | a `requires:` line that this host or this LLVM does not meet |
| `needs-toolchain` |  |  | 33 | 33 | `args:` use a placeholder the capture does not substitute (`%{gcc_toolchain}` and the like: a toolchain kiln's own suite locates) |
| `libc++` |  |  | 10 | 9 | `-stdlib=libc++`: the entry's link (`link: c++`) is against libstdc++ |
| `link-flags` |  |  | 5 | 5 | a link option the entry's link cannot repeat (`-l...`, `-fuse-ld=`, `-static`) |
| `opt-first-lto` |  |  | 3 | 3 | `-flto`: kiln++ gives llc nothing; the link runs the code generator |
| `opt-first-optimized` |  |  | 38 | 38 | `-O1` or higher: `opt` first, bitcode to llc |
| `opt-first-coroutine` |  |  | 25 | 25 | coroutines are lowered by `opt`: bitcode to llc |
| `opt-first-always-inline` |  |  | 31 | 31 | an `always_inline` function (most often a standard library one) makes kiln++ run `opt`: bitcode to llc |
| `compile-fails` |  |  | 1 | 1 | the producer fails before any module reaches llc |
| `clang-rejects` | 65 | 63 |  |  | clang does not accept the test (GNU C that only GCC compiles) |
| `special-flags` | 3 | 3 |  |  | the test asks for options the capture does not translate for clang |
| `link-fails` | 2 | 2 |  |  | the module compiles but the program does not link |
| `program-fails` | 7 | 7 |  |  | the program built with the real llc does not exit with status 0 in time |
| `not-reproducible` | 4 | 4 | 2 | 1 | the entry does not pass `irdiff` with every linker when llc alone builds it (see "Admission") |

### `llc` arguments

The arguments the producer's driver gave `llc` (without `-o <object>` and the input). `irdiff` builds an entry with `-O0 -filetype=obj -relocation-model=pic` or `static` (by the entry's `link:` line) and the module's own triple; arguments beyond those are recorded in the manifest and in the entry's header comment, and are not repeated by `irdiff`.

| llc arguments | `gcc-torture/llvm22` | `gcc-torture/llvm19` | `kiln/llvm22` | `kiln/llvm19` | repeated by irdiff |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `-O0 -relocation-model=pic -filetype=obj` | 1,672 | 1,674 | 1,218 | 1,184 | yes |
| `-O0 -relocation-model=pic -filetype=obj -debugger-tune=gdb` |  |  | 6 | 6 | no |

12 of 5,760 entries were built by their producer with `llc` arguments `irdiff` does not repeat.

## Census

The census is lexical. The scanner splits each module into tokens (comments, strings, `c"..."` constants and quoted names are single tokens and are never counted as code), joins lines into statements (a line continues the statement before it while a bracket is open, and when it starts with `to`, `catch`, `cleanup` or `filter` inside a function body), and reads only the parts of a statement that a table needs. Known approximations:

- A type is recognised where the grammar puts one (after an opcode, in a parameter list); type *mentions* (integer widths, floating-point kinds, vectors) are counted per token, so a constant's type counts as a mention.
- Named struct types are resolved to their shape for the by-value tables; struct literals and named types are not counted as type mentions.
- Constant expressions are recognised by their keyword followed by `(` at a position that is not the instruction's own opcode.
- `prefix` and `prologue` data on functions are counted but their constants are not read.
- Instruction counts exclude `#dbg_*` records. A basic block is a label line, plus the unlabelled entry block of a function.
- Module counts say in how many modules a row occurs at least once.

## Tests that are not in the corpus

Every test the capture saw and did not capture, by source and reason, with the LLVM majors it was skipped for.

### kiln tests that fail without hod

The capture builds each of kiln's executing tests (`expect: run`) with plain `kiln++` and the real `llc`, honouring the test's header (`args:`, `run-args:`, `run-stdin:`, `exit:`, `stdout:`, `requires:`, `xfail:`). A test that then does not build, link, run as its header says, or pass `irdiff` with every linker is a failure that has nothing to do with hod. These are all of them:

- `tests/conformance/expr.const/builtins-srcloc-path-style.cpp` (LLVM 22, 19): `compile-fails`: `kiln++: exit status 1: tests/conformance/expr.const/builtins-srcloc-path-style.cpp:48:15: error: static assertion failed due to requirement 'h_file[0] == '/''`
- `tests/conformance/dcl.struct.bind/p0963-binding-condition.cpp` (LLVM 22): `not-reproducible`: `with mold: oracle: link with mold failed (exit status 1): mold: error: symbol type mismatch: gets`
- `tests/conformance/over.match.copy/direct-init-explicit-conversion-to-copy-ctor.cpp` (LLVM 22, 19): `not-reproducible`: `with mold: oracle: link with mold failed (exit status 1): mold: error: symbol type mismatch: glob`

A runner that does *not* honour the header fails on more: every test under `multi-file`, `needs-toolchain`, `needs-env`, `marked-xfail` and most under `requires` below fails to build or run when its file alone is given to `kiln++` with the header's arguments verbatim, and a test with a `run-stdin:` line fails without its input. A C++ test also fails to link when the compiler is run under the name `kiln` instead of `kiln++` (the name selects the C++ driver and with it the C++ standard library at the link). Measured once over the 1540 run tests of kiln `bd60e182`, such a runner fails 176 of them, by cause in `spec/landed/harness/WP-017.md`.
